oneLiner: The purest public bet on the 2026 NAND supercycle - 84.6% gross margin and $39 of quarterly EPS at the peak - priced near 3x forward earnings because the entire debate is how long it can possibly last.
thesis: AI inference has structurally rewired NAND demand. Server eSSDs were 48% of industry bit shipments in Q2 CY2026; Sandisk datacenter revenue rose 437% in FY2026 and 103% QoQ in Q4, and the QLC Stargate platform began revenue shipments for high-capacity AI data lakes.

The NBM contract model attacks cyclicality head-on. Ten New Business Model agreements worth a minimum $93.9B with 4+ years of visibility have been signed, and management expects NBMs to cover 50%+ of FY2027 bits with locked pricing.

Supply discipline is holding. Capex stays near 6% of revenue, BiCS8 now carries the majority of bit production, and the Kioxia JV was extended to 2034 - the industry has not yet blinked into overbuild.
It is a cash machine returning capital. FY2026 GAAP net income was $11.43B on $20.25B revenue, and the buyback authorization was expanded to $15.5B.
Even heroic skepticism struggles with the multiple. At roughly 3.2x consensus FY2027 EPS, the market already assumes a violent margin collapse; anything less is upside.

latestProse: Q4 FY2026 (reported August 5) was a blowout: revenue of $8.965B rose 51% sequentially and 372% YoY, with roughly one-third of the sequential gain from volume and two-thirds from pricing - ASPs are still climbing. Non-GAAP gross margin reached 84.6% against a 79-81% guide, producing non-GAAP EPS of $39.25 (consensus $34.45). Datacenter revenue of $2,977M doubled sequentially to ~33% of sales (management cited datacenter at 38% of portfolio exiting the year vs 12% at the start). The disclosure that matters most: ten NBM long-term agreements totaling a minimum $93.9B, converting a spot-price cycle into contracted visibility.
guidanceProse: Q1 FY2027 guidance: revenue $10.3-10.8B, non-GAAP gross margin 83-85%, non-GAAP EPS $44-46 - record numbers that still read as deceleration, since sequential growth is now mostly volume with only modest price increases because NBM contracts lock pricing, and margin is guided down from 84.6% on mix and higher component costs. That is the headline debate: bulls see contracted visibility toward a NAND market management says exceeds $300B in CY2026 and approaches $500B in CY2027; bears see the moment ASP momentum stalls at the top of the cycle. The stock fell ~8% after hours on the guide.

guide.label: Q1 FY2027 revenue guide
guide.sub: Non-GAAP GM 83-85%, EPS $44-46; growth mostly volume as NBM pricing is locked

segments: Datacenter (enterprise SSD/AI): $2,977M, ~33% of Q4 revenue, +103% QoQ, +437% YoY for FY26 - mix was ~12% entering the fiscal year
Edge (client/mobile/OEM): $5,432M, ~61% of Q4 revenue, +48% QoQ on repricing
Consumer (retail cards/drives): $556M, ~6% and shrinking as bits shift to eSSD
competitive: Q2 CY2026 NAND share by shipments: Samsung 25%, SK Hynix 22%, YMTC 14% (top-3 for the first time), then Kioxia, Micron, and Sandisk sixth by volume - though Sandisk and Kioxia rank higher by revenue on richer eSSD mix
Kioxia is simultaneously JV partner (shared fabs, common BiCS roadmap, JV extended to 2034) and direct rival in enterprise SSD
Samsung and SK Hynix are diverting capex priority toward HBM/DRAM, a key reason NAND supply stayed tight; their re-entry appetite is the biggest swing factor
YMTC's volume surge is the wildcard supply threat, mitigated for now by its low eSSD share and export-control constraints
moat: NAND is a commodity: no supplier holds pricing power through a full cycle, and today's 84.6% margin is cycle rent, not moat. Sandisk's durable edges are cost/scale via the Kioxia JV and BiCS8/BiCS10 node leadership, plus - if they hold in a downturn - NBM contracts that convert spot exposure into multi-year committed volumes. The contracts are unproven in a falling-price environment.
risks: Peak-cycle margins are unprecedented and already guided down. No NAND maker has sustained 80%+ gross margin; the first quarter of falling ASPs will compress margins and the multiple simultaneously.
Double-ordering risk. Prior shortages ended when customers who double-ordered walked away; a $93.9B 'minimum' backlog built at panic pricing is exactly where that unwinds.
The supply response is coming. YMTC hit 14% shipment share, and $500B TAM forecasts are precisely the signal that historically triggers competitor capacity expansion into 2027-28 oversupply.
NBM enforceability is untested. Minimum-value, multi-year agreements have never been through a NAND downturn.
Kioxia JV dependence. Capacity and node-transition decisions are shared, not controlled, and BiCS10 execution risk is material.
Extreme expectations embedded in estimates. Consensus FY2027 EPS near $396 assumes shortage conditions persist all year; a modest ASP miss craters the E in the P/E.
catalysts: Late Oct/early Nov 2026: Q1 FY2027 earnings
Late Oct 2026: Samsung and SK Hynix Q3 CY2026 NAND capex commentary
Nov-Dec 2026: TrendForce/Counterpoint Q3 CY2026 NAND pricing and share data
Ongoing: additional NBM agreements and $15.5B buyback execution
pricedIn: SNDK traded at $1,266.50 on Aug 11, 2026, up ~574% over the past year but ~45% below its early-summer high near $2,350. The forward P/E is roughly 3.2x on consensus FY2027 EPS near $396 - the classic trough-multiple-on-peak-earnings memory setup. Consensus target is $2,054 (Strong Buy; range $1,000-3,000). The debate: if NBMs genuinely de-cyclicalize earnings the stock re-rates dramatically; if this is a normal cycle wearing contracts as a costume, 3x peak EPS is not cheap at all.

scenarios.bear: The cycle tops in FY2027: supply responds (YMTC, restarted Samsung/SK Hynix NAND capex), customers work down double-ordered inventory, NBM minimums get renegotiated, and ASPs roll; margins fall toward historical 30-40%, EPS collapses to a small fraction of consensus, and the stock overshoots down toward the pre-surge hundreds.
scenarios.base: Shortage conditions persist through CY2027 but pricing flattens; margins ease into the 70s, FY2027 non-GAAP EPS lands meaningfully below the $396 consensus but still very high, and the stock oscillates in the $1,200-1,800 range as the market refuses a full re-rating until NBMs survive a soft quarter.
scenarios.bull: AI storage demand keeps NAND undersupplied into CY2028, the ~$500B CY2027 TAM view proves roughly right, NBM coverage above 50% of bits holds pricing through wobbles; even at 5-6x the stock exceeds the $2,054 consensus target.

valPresets.note: Basis is forward earnings, MU-style: at ~3.2x forward the market prices a violent earnings decline - the reverse DCF quantifies the implied annual collapse rate. Only 3 years of standalone filings exist (Feb 2025 spin).
